vault.title: Lab 01 - Image basics (numpy)
vault.summary: This document outlines the first lab assignment for an Introduction to Computer Vision course, focusing on treating images as NumPy arrays. Students are required to construct a synthetic 64x64 RGB gradient image from scratch without external image files. The tasks include calculating channel statistics, converting the image to grayscale, performing array slicing for cropping and flipping, computing a 256-bin intensity histogram, and applying thresholding to generate an ASCII art visualization. The final deliverable is a Jupyter notebook submitted via WSP by Friday 23:59 of week 2.
key_terms: NumPy: A fundamental package for scientific computing with Python used for array manipulation.
RGB gradient: An image representation combining red, green, and blue color channels smoothly varying in intensity.
Grayscale: An image format where each pixel represents a single light intensity value.
Array slicing: A Python technique to extract subsets of multi-dimensional arrays without using loops.
Histogram: A graphical representation of the distribution of numerical data, such as pixel intensities.
Thresholding: A technique used to create binary images by setting pixels above a certain value to foreground.

vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision Syllabus
vault.summary: This document outlines the 15-week schedule, grading policy, and lab assignments for CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision, taught by Abenova Saule. Students will learn about image processing, feature detection, CNNs, and object detection. The course grade is based on labs (30%), a midterm (30%), and a final project (40%).
key_terms: Convolution: A mathematical operation used in image filtering.
Edge detection: Identifying points in an image where image brightness changes sharply.
SIFT: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform used for detecting and describing local features in images.
Homography: A transformation relating the points of one plane to another.
RANSAC: Random Sample Consensus algorithm for robust parameter estimation.
CNN: Convolutional Neural Network used for image classification and computer vision tasks.

vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision - Lecture 01
vault.summary: This introductory lecture outlines the course structure and grading criteria for Introduction to Computer Vision. Students learn how digital images are represented as multidimensional arrays defined by height, width, and channels with uint8 data types. Essential Python libraries including NumPy, OpenCV, and Matplotlib are introduced as the primary tooling for the course.
key_terms: Images as arrays: Digital images represented as numerical grids with height, width, and channels.
dtype uint8: 8-bit unsigned integer data type commonly used for pixel values ranging from 0 to 255.
numpy: A foundational Python library for numerical computing and array manipulations.
OpenCV: A widely used computer vision and image processing library in Python.
matplotlib: A plotting library used for visualizing images and data in Python.
